findings.evidence: l. 378 "as recorded for the `R_H2` block in the source" vs l. 21-22 "The three blocks have freely reduced lengths `80`, `160`, and `309`, giving the published total length `549`" and l. 200-201 "Free reduction gives block lengths 80, 160, and 309, agreeing with the source's total 549".
findings.fix: Either cite where the source records the per-block figures, or reword the three docstrings to say the block figures are computed by this transcription and only their sum 549 is the published figure.
findings.issue: The docstrings of `lyPresentation_reducedH2Length`, `lyPresentation_reducedH1Length` and `lyPresentation_reducedExtensionLength` say 80/160/309 are "as recorded for the R_H2/R_H1/R_G block in the source", but the module docstring (l. 21-22) and `transcriptionNotes` (l. 201) attribute only the total 549 to Gebhardt. One of the two is false; if the source publishes only the total, three of the four length theorems are decompositions of a single check dressed as independent source comparisons, which misleads the required independent source-to-Lean read-through.

findings.evidence: GroupPresentation.lean l. 153-155: "A published presentation length is normally measured after free and cyclic reduction of each relator, so this is what makes `totalLength` comparable with such a figure." Siblings prove it: ONan.lean:338, Suzuki.lean:285, Mathieu.lean:272, Fischer/TwentyThree.lean:193. Non-reducedness: Relator.lean l. 91-97 gives `toWord (.pow (.inv (conj c b)) 2) = [(b,false),(c,false),(b,true),(b,false),(c,false),(b,true)]`.
findings.fix: Add the decidable check `∀ w ∈ lyPresentation.relators, FreeGroup.IsCyclicallyReduced (FreeGroup.reduce w)` (the `FreeGroup.reduce` form, since the raw compiled words are not reduced) and say in the docstring/notes that this is what makes 549 comparable with the published length.
findings.issue: `lyPresentation_reducedTotalLength` is the row's only external cross-check, but nothing establishes it measures the published quantity. A published presentation length is measured after free *and cyclic* reduction (GroupPresentation.lean l. 132-133, 151-155), and this row proves no reducedness statement at all, unlike every other sporadic row. `relatorsCyclicallyReduced` is in fact false here: `.pow (.inv (Relator.conj c b)) 2` compiles to `b⁻¹c⁻¹b b⁻¹c⁻¹b`, and `div` joins cancel (relator 9's LHS ends in `b`, `invRev` of its RHS starts with `b⁻¹`), so `totalLength` is not 549 either. If any compiled word is freely reduced but not cyclically reduced, its source letter count is smaller and the 549 agreement is apples-to-oranges.

findings.evidence: l. 116-120: `Relator.div (Relator.sourceComm z (…)) (b ⬝ c ⬝ bInv ⬝ cInv)`; `Relator.toFreeGroup_sourceComm` (Relator.lean l. 238-242) gives `r⁻¹s⁻¹rs`, whereas the written word `b c b⁻¹ c⁻¹` is `⁅b,c⁆`. `sourceComm` is used for every other bracket in the file (l. 63, 64, 117).
findings.fix: Record in `transcriptionNotes` how the source prints this right-hand side; if it is bracketed, transcribe it as `Relator.sourceComm b c` (or `Relator.sourceComm (.inv b) (.inv c)` if barred), matching the treatment of the left side.
findings.issue: R_G relator 4 is the only relator whose *relation*, not merely its word, depends on the commutator convention, and it is transcribed inconsistently: the left side uses `Relator.sourceComm` (source convention `x⁻¹y⁻¹xy`) while the right side is the hand-written word `b c b⁻¹ c⁻¹`, which is Mathlib's `⁅b,c⁆` and equals the source's `[b̄,c̄]`, not the source's `[b,c] = b⁻¹c⁻¹bc`. If the source prints a bracket there, the transcribed relation is a different group element and the presented group is not Ly; no check in the module can detect this, since both candidate words have length 4 and the 549 total is unchanged.

summary: The transcription is structurally coherent and its internal checks are sound, but the three block-length theorems misattribute author-computed figures to the source, and the row's only external cross-check (total length 549) is not established to measure the same quantity as a published presentation length, since no reducedness property is proved and the compiled words are provably not freely reduced.
